profile.entities: CITI (Confederation of Indian Textile Industry); Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme (RIPS); customers in US/Europe/UK; competitors Bangladesh, Vietnam, China
profile.mgmt: Dinesh Nolkha (CMD), Nitin Nolakha (MD), P. Maheshwari (CFO); hosted by SMIFS (Awanish Chandra)
profile.subseg: Cotton & blended yarn; knitted fabric; woven (finished) fabric; exports
profile.themes: China+1 / export diversification (Europe-EU & UK FTAs driving sourcing shift to India); value-added fabric mix; US tariff normalization

bull_bear.body: Net D/E down to 0.76x (from 0.89x). Balance financing via internal accruals + debt. Peak/normal total debt ~INR1,900-2,000 cr post-project (incl WC). Avg cost of borrowing ~5.6% (term), WC <7%, blended ~6.5%. Dividend INR3/share (30%).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation (debt)

bull_bear.body:
- Cotton price: upward trend resuming; India-international parity dependence; lobbying for duty removal — outcome govt-dependent.
- China / export demand: West Asia/Iran-US conflict disrupting transit (esp. Europe) and freight; synthetic export logistics hit. US apparel inflation — a further 5-10% retail price rise could dent demand.
- Capex execution / ramp: H2 FY27 timing; ~INR1,900-2,000 cr peak debt.
- Knitted fabric: lost some US customers during tariff period; rebuild over 1-1.5 yrs.
- FTA timing slippage (EU another couple of quarters; duty removal uncertain).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident and measured. "Highest ever quarterly revenue," constructive on demand recovery, FTAs and spread sustainability; firmly declined hard margin/segment-margin guidance (consistent 16-20% range repeated). Realistic on macro/tariff/inflation ("quite a macro question, very difficult to predict"). Declined inventory disclosure.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- Spread INR90 floor should now be read as ~INR100 due to inflation in power/labor/component costs — re-rating of "normal" spread.
- China contribution to spread increase deliberately downplayed (10-11%→15-16% shipment share, not 30%+ of old) — mgmt won't attribute margin gain to China alone; restocking + transit-time fear + RM-cost floor are bigger drivers.
- Poly→cotton substitution thesis dismissed (cotton rose more than poly in INR/kg terms; poly still cheaper).
- Knit fabric weakness was tariff-driven (50% US tariff on low-value knits), now reversing.
- Renewable capex (INR230-240 cr) was unplanned add-on within the year.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging alongside growth: Net Debt to Equity Ratio 1.71 in FY16 versus 0.76 in FY26; the FY23-FY26 series is shown as 0.95, 1.17, 0.89, 0.76.
- "~Rs. 2,083 cr cash generated from operations over the 10 years"; Cash Flow from Operations 100 (FY16) to 411 (FY26) Rs. Crs, described as "~4.1x".
- Growth funded through reinvestment rather than equity: Gross Fixed Assets 625 (FY16) to 2,560 (FY26) Rs. Crs ("~4.1x"), with equity share capital flat at 56.2 Rs. Crs from Mar-23 through Mar-26.
- Stated philosophy: "Strive to improve market share with consistent and disciplined capex over the years" and "Disciplined capex and prudent working capital management are ensuring financial strength and supporting sustained profitability".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Demand improved in Q4 across both domestic and export — driven by US tariff removal, restocking across downstream channels, and longer transit times prompting earlier buying. H1 FY26 had demand destruction/underutilization from US tariff uncertainty; H2 hit by West Asia conflict (supply-chain disruption, higher freight/transit). Exports ~63% of Q4 revenue. India export of yarn ~100 mn kg/yr industry-wide expected to hold, with ~5-10% incremental demand (helped by China buying more). China share of Nitin's shipments rose 10-11% → 15-16% in March (was 30%+ four years back).
business.title: Demand

business.body:
- **Yarn (74% FY26):** Cotton + blended/synthetic. Spread ~INR120-125/kg. Synthetic (pure) margins static; blended (PC/cotton-blended) margins improved. Polyester prices +20%+ post-war; cotton +INR30-35/kg over 3 months (polyester +INR25-27/kg) — no advantage to shift poly→cotton currently. Synthetic blended exports (PV, etc.) to Asia/Middle East/Africa hit by logistics, creating domestic oversupply pressure.
- **Fabric (21-22% FY26):** Woven ~18% (errata; said 20%), knitted ~4% (errata; said 2-3%). Fabric prices move with a lag — March yarn increases now translating into fabric; knit realization +~5% QoQ, woven +~2-2.5% QoQ. **Finished fabric margins structurally superior to yarn margins.** Knitted fabric production was DOWN (heavy US exposure, low-value item hit by 50% tariff); recovering as tariff normalizes — normal 65-70% utilization expected back in ~1-1.5 yrs.
business.title: Segment (yarn / fabric)

business.body:
- ✅ Beneficiary of US tariff normalization (10% vs feared 20-50%) and demand restocking.
- ⭐ Structural beneficiary of India-UK & India-EU FTAs (duty-disadvantage elimination, China+1 sourcing diversification to India) — finished-fabric and yarn demand uplift.
- ⭐ Beneficiary of domestic capacity rationalization (obsolete spinning capacity exited) supporting sustainable spreads.

---
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries

business.body:
- Established 1992 with "30+ Years of Experience"; ISO 9001:2015 certified, exporting to "55+ Countries" spanning six continents, which the deck says gives "Well-diversified export presence across all continents" and "mitigat[es] risks from regional volatility".
- Integrated yarn-to-fabric player: two Rajasthan plants (Bhilwara and Chittorgarh) with "State-of-the-art European & Global Manufacturing Machinery", the Chittorgarh site described as an "Integrated Textiles Complex" with spinning, weaving plus dyeing, printing and finishing.
- Export leadership externally validated: TEXPROCIL "Gold Trophy for Highest Exports of Cotton Yarn of Counts 50s and below in Category III for the year 2022-2023" and "Gold Plaque for Highest Exports of Cotton Yarn of Counts 51s and above in Category I"; also "Gold Trophy for Highest Employment Generation (Overall)" for 2022-23 and 2023-24.
- Deck's product-mix framing for Q1FY27: Yarn 72.4%, Fabrics 21.6%, Others 6.0% of total revenue; geography Domestic 34.8% / Export 65.2%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Industry outlook] Management states "The long-term outlook for the Indian textile industry remains positive, supported by various trade agreements and policy measures, as well as improved price parity between international and domestic cotton."
- [Guidance] CMD Mr. Dinesh Nolkha: "we remain confident of delivering year-on-year growth for the full year FY27, supported by the commercialization of our additional capacities of fabric and yarn".
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Cotton: international ~$0.63-0.64/lb and domestic INR52,000-55,000/candy were 3-4 yr lows till Dec'25; now trending up but India-international parity holds. Govt removed cotton import duty Aug-Dec'25 (industry pushing for permanent/another removal).
- Gas-based yarn very small; gas cost ~1.7x vs Feb but immaterial and passed on (global phenomenon).
- Power: renewable footprint expanding — Q4 added 10 MW hybrid PPA (INR9.5 cr, operational Q3'27); ~75 MW renewable added in year incl PPAs → near 100 MW total; 50-55% of present+future power from renewables. Savings ~INR50 cr/annum at full ramp.
- Freight: sea freight to Europe +75-80% vs Feb, rest of world +15-20%; mostly passed on (FOB sales); transit +~2 weeks. Already factored in numbers (normalized since March).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost (cotton, power)

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Record revenue INR859.8 cr (+7.4% QoQ); EBITDA margin 15.17% (+124 bps QoQ); PAT INR57.4 cr (+29.2% QoQ); yarn spread ~INR110→~INR125/kg; net D/E 0.76x. Capex >INR300 cr of ~INR1,100 cr spent, commercializes H2 FY27 (fabric Oct-Dec, spinning Jan-Feb). FY27 guide: 16-20% margin range; +30-35% revenue over time. Renewable ~75 MW added, ~INR30-35 cr savings this year. Errata: fabric capacity to ~75 mn m (not 70); woven 18%, knit 4% of revenue.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Margin:** Normalized EBITDA margin range **16%-20%** (product profile dependent); expects to fall in that range in **FY27**. (Mgmt declined a hard number but engaged questioners on 17-18% scenario.)
- **Yarn spread:** ~INR120-125/kg viewed as sustainable "median"; floor now ~INR100 (inflation-adjusted from INR90).
- **Volume / utilization:** Spinning ~97-98%, fabric 90%+ to continue for next 2 quarters until new capacity arrives (some summer dip due to heat).
- **Capex ramp:** New capacity commercializes H2 FY27 — fabric (Oct-Dec'26), spinning (Jan-Feb'27); renewable power H2. Asset turn ~1:1 on new capex (1.2-1.3x company-wide ex-renewable).
- **Capacity ramp:** Spinning +22,000 t → ~130,000 t; fabric +35 mn m → ~75 mn m (errata-corrected). End-to-end finished/value-added fabric.
- **Top line:** Capex should add >INR1,000 cr revenue; yarn-price normalization adds ~5-7% of existing turnover; combined mgmt expects to add **~30-35%** to existing revenue going forward.
- **Renewable savings:** ~INR50 cr/annum at full ramp; ~INR30-35 cr in current year (~1% of margin).
- **Peak/total debt:** ~INR1,900-2,000 cr including working capital post-project.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- Large integrated capex (spinning +22k t, fabric +35 mn m) commercializing H2 FY27; completely integrated end-to-end finished fabric (value-add).
- Mix shift toward value-added/finished fabric to improve structural margin.
- **FTAs as optionality:** India-UK FTA "to fructify soon" (eliminates duty disadvantage vs competitors); India-EU FTA ~couple quarters out — big boost; European brands already inquiring/planning to diversify sourcing to India (China+1 / geopolitical-stability play). New Zealand FTA + existing Australia presence = geographic expansion.
- Decade track record: revenue/EBITDA/PAT grown ~3-4x; >INR2,000 cr cumulative CFO.
- Future capex: "many things on the drawing board," no number yet.
outlook.title: Growth / Optionality

deepdive.thesis: Vertically-integrated cotton/blended yarn + fabric exporter delivering record quarterly revenue on demand recovery and yarn-spread expansion (~INR125/kg), with a large ~INR1,100 cr capex (spinning +22k t to ~130k t; fabric +35 mn m to ~75 mn m) commercializing H2 FY27 that should lift top line ~30-35% and shift mix toward higher-margin value-added/finished fabric.

open.item: No major volume growth expected in FY26; only very small gains from modernisation. Announced capex fructifies in FY27.
FY26 earnings driver will be cost efficiencies, better product mix and modernisation rather than volume, given capacity constraints.
No major volume growth expected in the next 12 months as spinning runs ~97% and fabric ~90%+; only minor debottlenecking/knitting gains until new capacity comes in FY27.
After renewable additions, ~50-55% of present and future power requirement to be met by renewable energy.
Additional INR9.5 crore investment for a 10 MW hybrid PPA (announced Q4FY25) to be operational by Q3 FY27; total renewable additions ~75 MW during year, taking total power capacity near 100 MW.
Ongoing capex to commercialize in H2 FY27: fabric from Oct-Dec 2026, spinning by Jan-Feb 2027; adds fabric to ~75 million meters and spinning to ~130,000 tons.
Company expects to fall into its normal 16-20% EBITDA margin range in FY27, up from FY26's 14.09%, driven by better realizations and value addition.
Company expects India's ~100 million kg/month yarn exports to be maintained, with possible ~5-10% incremental international demand from China restocking.
Total debt (incl. working capital) expected to peak at ~INR1,900-2,000 crore after the project; net D/E already down to 0.76x.
Company expects to add ~30-35% to existing revenue: ~INR1,000+ crore from the INR1,100 cr capex plus ~5-7% from yarn price normalization/recoupment.
New fabric capacity expected to ramp to at least 80% utilisation in FY28; company targets asset turn ~1:1 on new capex (ex-renewable), company-wide ~1.2-1.3x.
Industry (via CITI) pushing government to permanently remove cotton import duty; management expects an interim 6-month removal likely within 6 months.
Given EU FTA and US trade deal, company may look at garments even without PLI, but only after establishing new fabric capacity; no definitive plan yet.
Renewable investments expected to save ~INR50 crore per annum once fully fructified, and ~INR30-35 crore during FY27.
Company expanding export reach; New Zealand FTA and Australia presence flagged as focus areas to grow export business.
Spinning capex ex-fabric is ~INR600 crore of the INR1,120 crore project (rest fabric/spinning split).
Company (via industry/government committee) is working to improve cotton productivity per acre; results expected in ~1-2 years.
No definitive plans to enter garmenting yet; may consider after establishing the new fabric capacity given EU/US FTA market opening.
Company targets IRR of ~14-15% on the INR1,120 crore capex.
New capacity across yarn/weaving/processing will also handle synthetic (man-made) fibers; company can pivot to synthetics if better margins emerge.

verdicts.note: 'removal of tariffs by U.S.A'; 'they were planning for a duty of about 20%... getting only a duty of 10%' - the tariff uncertainty resolved relatively favorably for India after a volatile period.

verdicts.note: 'over the last decade, we have grown our revenue, EBITDA and PAT by nearly 3 to 4x'; 'add 30% to 35% to our existing revenue' - growth strategy reaffirmed (decade CAGR ~14-15%, below the 18-19% earlie…

verdicts.item: Short-term no major margin driver; company will pursue cost efficiency, product-mix and value addition. Normal aspirational margin is 16-20%, currently ~300 bps below.
verdicts.note: 'our normal margin should be in the range of 16% to 20%. We expect... to fall into this level during... FY 27' - Q4 15.17% approaching, still below-normal in FY26 (14.09%). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: ~INR50 crore of modernization to be spent this calendar year; major capacity expansion only in next financial year.
